title: Can a trapezium be broken into a rectangle and two triangles?
description: Two straight lines come down from the top corners of a trapezium and cut it into a rectangle and two end triangles. The three areas are added, and the same number comes from the rule with half, the height and the two parallel sides. Keeko doubts this and multiplies the long side by the height, which fills a rectangle with two empty corners.
teaching_notes: One idea: a trapezium is a rectangle in the middle and a triangle at each end, so its area is the sum of three areas. Watch for students who take the long parallel side times the height.

source: Trapezium WXYZ with WX parallel to ZY, split by WM and XN perpendicular to ZY into a rectangle and two triangles
video_script.why: The child knows the areas of rectangles and triangles and builds the area of a trapezium from them, as the book does.
video_script.substitution: Numbers for the book's trapezium WXYZ: WX = 5, ZY = 9, height 4, ZM = 2 and NY = 2.
video_script.anchor: the trapezium WXYZ of the book with WM and XN dropped to ZY
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko multiplies the long parallel side nine by the height four and says the area is thirty six square units. That is the rectangle round the trapezium, with two empty corner triangles of four square units each.
video_script.payoff_line: The trapezium covers twenty eight square units.
maths_rules: WX = 5, ZY = 9, height WM = XN = 4, ZM = 2, NY = 2; check 2 + 5 + 2 = 9
rule: 1/2 x height x (sum of parallel sides) = 1/2 x 4 x (5 + 9) = 1/2 x 4 x 14 = 28
video_script.design: One trapezium WXYZ stays all video, split into a rectangle in the middle and a triangle at each end in two colours. The rule with half is written under the sum as a check. Keeko's rectangle is drawn round the same shape.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a trapezium W X Y Z.
<bookmark mark='top'/>The top side W X is five units long.
<bookmark mark='bottom'/>The bottom side Z Y is nine units, and the height between them is four units.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many square units does the trapezium cover?

beats.on_screen: the trapezium stays on the board and Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: lines WM and XN drop from W and X to ZY; the rectangle WXNM is shaded in one colour and the two end triangles in a second colour, with ZM = 2 and NY = 2 marked

marks.drop: the lines WM and XN drop from W and X to ZY
marks.ends: the two end triangles are shaded in a second colour with ZM = 2 and NY = 2

beats.colours: rectangle in one colour, triangles in a second colour
narration: <bookmark mark='drop'/>Draw W M and X N straight down to Z Y, at right angles to it.
<bookmark mark='rect'/>W X N M has four right angles, so it is a rectangle.
<bookmark mark='ends'/>Two triangles are left, one at each end, and each has a base of two units.

beats.on_screen: Given: WX = 5 units, ZY = 9 units, height 4 units, ZM = 2 units, NY = 2 units

marks.given: WX = 5, ZY = 9 and the height 4 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, W X is five units, Z Y is nine units and the height is four units.
<bookmark mark='ends'/>Z M and N Y are two units each.

beats.on_screen: To find: area of trapezium WXYZ

marks.find: the words area of trapezium WXYZ are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the area of the trapezium W X Y Z.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: rectangle WXNM, area = length × breadth = 5 × 4 = 20 square units

marks.rect: the rectangle WXNM lights up and the rule length × breadth is written
marks.val: 5 × 4 = 20 square units is written inside the rectangle

narration: <bookmark mark='rect'/>Step one, find the rectangle. Its area is length times breadth, five times four.
<bookmark mark='val'/>That gives twenty square units.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: each end triangle, area = 1/2 × base × height = 1/2 × 2 × 4 = 4 square units

marks.tri: one end triangle lights up and the rule 1/2 × base × height is written with the values 2 and 4
marks.val: 4 square units is written in each end triangle

narration: <bookmark mark='tri'/>Step two, find each end triangle. Its area is half times base times height, so half times two times four.
<bookmark mark='val'/>Each triangle has four square units.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: area WXYZ = triangle + rectangle + triangle = 4 + 20 + 4

marks.add: the three pieces slide together and the words triangle + rectangle + triangle are written

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add the three areas, because they fill the whole trapezium.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Four plus twenty plus four.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check with the rule, area = 1/2 × height × (sum of parallel sides) = 1/2 × 4 × (5 + 9)

marks.rule: the rule 1/2 × height × (sum of parallel sides) is written
marks.vals: the values 4, 5 and 9 replace the words

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step four, check with the rule from your book. Area is half times height times the sum of the parallel sides.
<bookmark mark='vals'/>Half times four times five plus nine.

beats.on_screen: Answer: area of trapezium WXYZ = 28 square units, both ways

marks.ans: the answer 28 square units is boxed
marks.both: the two working lines are joined by an equals sign

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The trapezium covers twenty eight square units.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Adding the pieces and using the rule give the same area.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the trapezium
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble reads 9 × 4 = 36; a rectangle 9 by 4 is drawn round the trapezium; the two empty corner triangles at the top are shaded in the warning colour

marks.box: a rectangle 9 by 4 is drawn round the trapezium
marks.corners: the two empty corner triangles at the top are shaded in the warning colour
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and 36 - 4 - 4 is written

beats.colours: warning colour for the empty corners
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we take the long side times the height, which is thirty six square units.
<bookmark mark='box'/>But nine by four is the rectangle round the whole trapezium.
<bookmark mark='corners'/>It has two empty corners at the top, and each corner is a triangle of four square units.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Take those two corners away from thirty six, and the area is twenty eight.
